audit_result.proof_trace: All price consumers in the health-check and eligibility paths use `get_price` (EMA) or `get_price_with_check` (EMA+spot spread), enforcing EMA staleness. However, `liquidate_calculate_seize_ctokens` calls `get_spot_price` for both debt and collateral prices (L1045-1046), checking only spot staleness — not EMA staleness. Because EMA and spot can diverge in value (EMA lags by design), when Pyth spot transiently exceeds the EMA, the seize amount is inflated relative to the EMA-based framework used for eligibility, granting liquidators collateral beyond the protocol's stated incentive.
audit_result.attack_scenario: A liquidator monitors Pyth price feeds and times their liquidation call when the debt asset's spot price is temporarily elevated above its EMA (normal during upward market momentum). The eligibility check passes on EMA prices; the seize amount is computed on inflated spot prices, extracting additional collateral from the borrower beyond the intended liquidation incentive without any flash-loan or oracle compromise.

PROP-current-fina-asm-005.text: System assumes Pyth oracle feed is not compromised; all consumers must apply EMA staleness checks.
PROP-current-fina-asm-005.assertion: assume: forall price_feed: NOT stale(price_feed) AND NOT manipulated(price_feed)
